Original Russian Text © V.V. Abashev, D.V. Metelkin, N.E. Mikhal’tsov, V.A. Vernikovsky, N.Yu. Matushkin, 2017, published in Fizika Zemli, 2017, No. 5, pp. 63–80.
Paleomagnetism of the Upper Paleozoic
of the Novaya Zemlya Archipelago
V. V. Abasheva, b, *, D. V. Metelkina, b, N. E. Mikhal’tsova, b, V. A. Vernikovskya, b, and N. Yu. Matushkina, b
aNovosibirsk State University, Novosibirsk, 630090 Russia
bTrofimuk Institute of Petroleum Geology and Geophysics, Siberian Branch,
Russian Academy of Sciences, Novosibirsk, 630090 Russia
*e-mail: abashevvv@ipgg.sbras.ru
Received March 10, 2017
Abstract⎯ The rock magnetic and paleomagnetic results from the Upper Paleozoic sedimentary sequences
composing the isles of the Novaya Zemlya Archipelago are presented. The recorded temperature depen-
dences of the magnetic susceptibility, the magnetic hysteresis parameters, and the results of the first-order
reversal curve (FORC) measurements suggest the presence of single-domain or pseudo-single-domain mag-
netite and hematite grains in the rocks. The Upper Paleozoic deposits overall are promising for unraveling the
tectonic evolution of the Barents–Kara region. Together with the rock magnetic data, the positive fold and
reversal tests testify to the primary origin of the indentified magnetization components. However, the inter-
pretation of the paleomagnetic data should take into account the probable inclination shallowing. New sub-
stantiation is offered for the paleomagnetic poles for Early Devonian and Late Permian. For the first time,
paleomagnetic constraints are obtained for the Late Carboniferous boundary. It is shown that the Early Cim-
merian deformation stage within the Paikhoi–Novaya Zemlya region is associated with the sinistral strike slip
displacement along the Baidaratskii suture during which the internal structure of the Southern Novaya Zem-
lya segment could undergo shear in addition to the nappe-thrust transformations. The Northern Novaya
Zemlya segment, which is shifted northwest with respect to the Southern segment, was deformed in the
thrusting mode with an overall clockwise rotation of this segment relative to the East European Craton.
Keywords: rock magnetism, paleomagnetism, Paleozoic, paleomagnetic pole, magnetotectonics, shear defor-
mations, Barents–Kara shelf, Novaya Zemlya Archipelago, the Arctic
DOI: 10.1134/S1069351317050019

ment rocks; (2–4) Early Paleozoic passive continental margin deposits for Southern Novaya Zemlya segment (SNZ) and Ven-
dian–Early Paleozoic age for Northern Novaya Zemlya segment (NNZ): (2) carbonate and carbonate-terrigenous shelf deposits,
(3) flysch-like and turbidite rocks of continental slope and continental rise; (4) terrigenous shelf and coastal-marine; (5–6) Late
Paleozoic–Early Mesozoic passive continental margin deposits; (5) flysch-like and turbidite rocks of continental slope and con-
tinental rise; (6) terrigenous shelf and coastal-marine rocks; (7) Triassic molasse; (8–9) occurrences of Paleozoic intraplate mag-
matism: (8) related to rifting; (9) related to trap magmatism; (10) astroblemes; (11) (a) large thrusts and (b) Baidaratskii (BR)
collisional suture; dashed line shows their presumed continuation. Letter denotations: NNZA, Northern Novaya Zemlya anti-
form; SNZA, Southern Novaya Zemlya antiform, including Vaigach–Novaya Zemlya (VNZ) and Pai-Khoi (PKh) highs;
troughs: KT, Kara Trough and KRT, Korotaikha Trough; and depressions: KAR, Kara Depression; KRD, Karamakuly Depres-
sion; and PNZ, Pre-Novaya Zemlya Depression.

(1)Quaternary pebblestones, sands, clays, and peat; (2) Lower Triassic Sedoyakhskaya Formation: sandstones and siltstones; (3) Upper
Permian Gysinaya Zemlya Formation: mudstones, siltstones, sandstones; (4) Upper Permian Gusinaya Zemlya Formation: mudstones,
siltstones, sandstones; (5) Lower and Upper Permian Eksovskaya Formation: mudstones, siltstones, sandstones; (6) Middle Carbonif-
erous–Lower Permian Barentsevskaya Formation: sandstones, mudstones; (7) Middele Carboniferous Kseninskaya stratum: mud-
stones, sandstones; (8) unstratified Lower–Middle Ledyanaya Gavan and Kaprizninskaya formations: limestones, mudstones, silt-
stones; (9)Lower Carboniferous Goryakovskaya Formation: carbonate breccia, limestones, calcarenites; (10) Lower Carboniferous
Goryakovskaya Formation: carbonate breccia, limestones, calcarenites; (11) unstratified Upper Devonian Voroninskaya and Karbas-
nikovskaya formations: limestones, mudstones, and dolomites; (12) Middle–Upper Devonian conglomerate formation: conglomerates
and sandstones, limestones; (13) Middle Devonian Chukhnovskaya Formation: mudstones, siltstones, limestones; (14) Lower Devo-
nian Retovskaya Formation: dolomites and limestones; (15) unstratified Lower Devonian Ermolaevskaya, Kan’onnaya, and Vesel-
ogorskaya formations: sandstones, siltstones, mudstones; (16) unstratified Upper Silurian–Lower Devonian Otkupshchikovskaya For-
mation: limestones, siltstones; (17) unstratified Lower–Upper Silurian Chaevskaya and Usachevskaya formations: siltstones, limestones,
sandstones; (18) geological boundaries: (a), stratigraphic; (b), tectonic; (19) paleomagnetic sampling points.
